messages:
zeke (Design): quick thread: prototype for keys page empty state + bulk revoke copy. two calls: 1) empty state microcopy and CTA hierarchy, 2) bulk revoke confirmation pattern (typed confirm vs undoable toast). thoughts?

ivy (PM): empty state should be friendly for non-devs. avoid jargon. suggested heading: "Create your first API key" body: "Generate a key to start integrating Redwood Inference. Keep it secret — youll only see it once." Primary CTA: "Create key" secondary: "Learn about key scopes".

harry (Eng): sounds good. tiny flag: we already map 'Create key' to 'c' keyboard shortcut on other pages. adding global shortcut here could conflict with in-browser shortcuts. maybe keep shortcut but only active when list has focus.

maya (A11y): agree on content. tiny copy nit: use "you'll" not "youll" (typo). also ensure CTA order for keyboard users: primary should be first in DOM for Tab order. For the secret reveal modal: keep modal open after create, auto-select secret, and show an inline helper with aria-live="polite" that says "Secret copied" after copy.

zeke (Design): fixed typo, thanks. for empty state visual: big icon, short bullets: "1) Create key 2) Assign role 3) Start calling the API". CTA stack: Create (primary) then Learn (text link). For accessibility, we'll ensure the Learn link is keyboard reachable.

ivy (PM): bulk revoke: product concern is safety. often infra teams accidentally bulk revoke a dev token. prefer typed confirmation if more than 5 keys selected. otherwise a reversible toast undo for 1-4 keys. this balances safety and speed.

harry (Eng): typed confirm complexity: we can validate input like typing the word REVOKE or the number of keys. it's doable. for <=4 keys, show modal with action and show toast with Undo for 10s; for >=5 require typing "REVOKE" to enable final CTA. Implementation note: keep the focus on the text input after opening the confirm modal; set aria-describedby with the list count.

maya (A11y): typed confirmation must be accessible. label the input clearly and provide an aria-live region that reads validation state (e.g., "Confirmation text entered"). Also don't rely on color. For the undo toast, ensure it is reachable by keyboard and has role="status" or aria-live="polite" but not assertive. Also ensure screen readers can reach the undo control (focusable).

zeke (Design): small mock updates: empty state copy as above, modal stays open after create with auto-selected secret and a small message: "This is the only time youll see this key. Copy it now." Bulk revoke: for 1-4 keys show modal + toast undo; for 5+ show typed confirm: label: "Type REVOKE to confirm revoking 7 keys" (count injected). We'll show a short explanation: "Revoked keys stop traffic immediately. This cannot be undone."

harry (Eng): sounds good. one more edge: when typed confirm fails validation, ensure SRs get instant feedback via aria-live region and a clear error message like "Text does not match; please type REVOKE exactly."

maya (A11y): agreed. also consider a feature for org admins: show a scaffolded warning when selecting cross-environment keys (prod + staging) with a bold line: "Warning: some selected keys are used in production" and an additional checkbox to confirm you understand. link to docs. That will reduce accidental mass outages.

ivy (PM): nice idea. let's include a small production badge in the key row so users can see environment flags before selecting. add confirm if any selected keys have prod badge. For copy: "Some keys in your selection are used in production. Revoking them will stop live services. Please confirm by typing REVOKE."

ci-bot: CI passed for branch feature/keys-empty-bulk-guard (artifact 2028-04-05T16:10Z).

zeke (Design): I'll update figma and push copy PR. meeting invite for short review after PR lands. thanks everyone :sparkles:

harry (Eng): happy to pair on the typed confirm accessibility wiring.

maya (A11y): I'll join and bring a checklist (focus order, aria-live messages, keyboard reachable undo toast, color contrast).

ivy (PM): good wrap. pairing after PR.
